The Democracy and Political Violence Collaborative is hosting a mini-conference
(a "conference within a conference") during MPSA's 2027 annual meeting on **Saturday, April 3**.
This is our second meeting, following our [pre-conference at APSA 2026](../apsa2026/index.qmd).

## What we're looking for

As always, we invite work — regardless of discipline, subfield, career stage, or approach —
that studies democracy and political violence, broadly construed. This includes, but is not
limited to, work on:

- democratic resilience and backsliding
- support for political violence and antidemocratic policies
- the effect of violence on political behavior

We welcome submissions of all kinds, including **abstracts, research plans, and papers**.

## Format

The day will feature three paper panels, a roundtable on the state of the field and avenues for
future research, and a reception and poster session. The rough schedule:

1. Coffee hour
2. Session 1
3. Session 2
4. Lunch
5. Session 3
6. Roundtable
7. Reception / poster session

While the conference focuses on accepted papers, **attendance and discussion are open with
advance registration**. Beyond the paper sessions, the day is structured to build an enduring
community of researchers in this space, with dedicated time for all attendees — presenters and
non-presenters alike — to connect, exchange ideas, and lay the groundwork for future
collaboration.

We expect all attendees to read the accepted papers, and accepted authors will also serve as
discussants.

## How to apply

Use the [application form](https://forms.gle/N8DT9HGRhqTAmciH9){target="_blank"} to submit
work or to register your interest in attending. The form requires a Google account to upload
files.

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## Applying to MPSA as well?
You can apply to present both at our mini-conference and at MPSA more generally. The two
processes are separate: we handle submissions to the mini-conference directly, and general
submissions are handled by MPSA.
:::

Questions, or just want to connect? Reach out to [the organizers](../about.qmd).
